chunks: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Ali ibn Abdullah al-Basri narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Hasan ibn Bandar al-Tamimi al-Tabari narrated to us in Asfarayn in the Congregation Mosque, saying: Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Tusi narrated to us in Tabaran, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Khashram al-Maruzi narrated to us, saying: Al-Fadl ibn Musa al-Sinani al-Maruzi narrated to us, saying: Abu Hanifa al-Nu'man ibn Thabit said to me: Shall I benefit you with an unusual narration which you have not heard the like of anything more unusual?

I said: Yes. Then Abu Hanifa said: Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman informed me, from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, from Abdullah ibn Bahiyyah, from Zaid ibn Thabit, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: O Zaid, have you married? I said: No. He said: Marry, and you will be virtuous after your chastity, and do not marry five. Zaid said: And who are they, O Messenger of Allah? The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: Do not marry a Shahbara, nor a Lahbara, nor a Nahbara, nor a Haydara, nor a Lafut. Zaid said: O Messenger of Allah, I do not know anything of what you mentioned, and I am ignorant of the last of them. Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said: Are you not Arabs? As for the Shahbara, she is the blue and vulgar. As for the Lahbara, she is the tall and gaunt. As for the Nahbara, she is the short and deformed. As for the Haydara, she is the old woman who is managed. As for the Lafut, she is the one with children from other than you.

key_terms.شَهْبَرَة: A type of woman, described as blue-eyed and vulgar
key_terms.لَفُوت: A type of woman, described as having children from another man
key_terms.لَهُبَرَة: A type of woman, described as tall and gaunt
key_terms.نَهْبَرَة: A type of woman, described as short and deformed
key_terms.هَيْدَرَة: A type of woman, described as an old woman who is managed

ai.seo_question: What are the five types of women mentioned in the hadith that one should not marry according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: This narration, transmitted through the chain of Abu Hanifa in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, highlights the Prophet’s practical guidance on marital compatibility by categorizing women based on physical and social traits using distinctive Arabic descriptors. While the terms (Shahbara, Lahbara, etc.) are often interpreted as specific archetypes of beauty or character flaws, the hadith underscores the importance of discernment in marriage to ensure harmony and prevent future discord. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Prophet’s wisdom in addressing both aesthetic preferences and practical realities of family life.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Abu’l-Hasan, Muhammed bin Amru bin Ali bin Abdullah al-Basri, that he said: We were told by Abu’l-Hasan, Ali bin Hasan bin Bandar al-Tamimi al-Tabari, in Esfarayen, in the mosque of the congregation, that he said: We were told by Abu Nasr, Muhammed bin Yusuf al-Tusi, in Tabaran [1], that he said: We were told by my father, that he said: We were told by Ali ibn Khashram al-Maruzi, that he said: We were told by Fadl bin Musa al-Nasa’I al-Maruzi, that he said: Abu Hanifa, Nu’man bin Thabit, said to me: Shall I benefit you with an unusual narration which you have not heard the like of anything more unusual?

He said: Then I said: Yes. Then Abu Hanifa said: I was informed by Hammad bin Sulayman, from Ibrahim al-Nakha’I, from Abdullah bin Najiya, from Zaid bin Thabit, that he said: The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said: O Zaid, have you married? I said: No. He said: Marry, and you will be virtuous after your chastity, and do not marry five. Zaid said: And who are they, O Messenger of Allah? The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said: Do not marry a shahbara, nor a lahbara, nor a nahbara, nor a haydara, nor a lafout. Zaid said: O Messenger of Allah, I do not know about anything of what you mentioned, and I am ignorant of the last of them. Then the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said: Are you not Arabs? As for the shahbara, she is the blue and vulgar. As for the lahbara, she is the tall and gaunty. As for the nahbara, she is the short and deformed. As for the haydara, she is the old woman who is managed. As for the lafout, she is the one with children from other than you.
